definition: one owner behaving differently on two products, and grading each separately

settled:
Google Fiber gets a C from me and Gmail gets a D, and Google owns both. That is the cleanest worked case I have.

The letter follows what they do on the one product. On the connection the price is steady, there are no ads inside the service, and I see no hard extraction of my data. On the things they sell my attention through, I see all three.

What the owner does elsewhere still sets how closely I watch. One line going bad is the leading sign for the rest of them.

So the unit I grade is not always the whole company, any more than it is always the whole institution behind one good practitioner.

Lifting a product above its owner takes concrete evidence on that product. Absent that, it takes the owner's grade. Google Search and Audible both take their owner's D, and what each of them does on its own pushes the same way.

title: The Same Company At Two Grades
